scientific_scope_status: In a finite undirected network with supplied c_e>0 and terminals A,B, an admissible potential u_A=0,u_B=1 orients an exactly conserved unit flow j_e>=0 along strictly positive drops Delta_e. No incoming flow at A or outgoing flow at B is allowed; zero-drop edges require zero flow. Discrete integration by parts gives sum j_e Delta_e=1. Draw a path by normalized outgoing flows, then a uniform potential level: its crossing edge has q_e=j_e Delta_e. Acquiring/checking the graph, outgoing tables, conservation, monotonicity and paths is charged; explicit input generally costs O(|E|). This reconstructs classical principles, not a new variational theorem.
